name: Karl Novak

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI firms, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. What happens on your factory shift?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Karl, 58, and I run an injection-moulding press that makes plastic pipe fittings. I earned a vocational machine-operations certificate and have spent twelve years on this press. I can adjust a normal cycle and spot a short shot or flash; a fitter handles the electrical cabinet.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How do your finances and technology habits fit together?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife Clara works at a community pharmacy counter, and our grown children run their own households. My night premium puts my operator wage above the usual rate, we have about a year's expenses saved, and there are plenty of plastics factories nearby. I use AI every day to find the right manual page and organise fault notes, then verify the mould setting from the approved sheet and test part. I like trying useful controls early, especially when a skilled operator teaches them hands-on. I value paid apprenticeships and family responsibility; Clara and I have not yet measured retirement income against our actual costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AI can improve the purchasing forecast if the right resin actually reaches my press. I would still measure the first fitting before approving a full moulding run.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our high night-rate wage, Clara's pay and a year saved cover current costs. Office AI does not change the mould cycle or my hands on the floor, so I do not see an immediate threat to my shift. A cleaner delivery plan would be a help if it prevents wrong resin bags.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep setting the moulding press and inspecting the first fitting for flash and missing plastic. I would continue my daily AI manual searches and fault-note summaries, checking every proposed setting against the approved sheet. From full paid night months I would add fresh wages to savings after household bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. A spreadsheet can order resin, but it cannot make a short fitting fit a pipe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does a short shot look like?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A corner of the fitting is not fully filled and its wall comes out thin. I stop the run and check the resin and cycle with the setter before we fill a carton.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why use AI every day if you check the manual?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It finds the relevant page faster and sorts my rough fault notes. The approved setting and a measured part still decide what I do at the press.

say: A better **resin forecast** still needs measured first fittings from every production run.
The actual **mould cycle** remains an operator's task.
think: Our **night premium** and one-year reserve cover current household costs.
Office AI does not yet remove my **physical press shift**.
do: **Keep** setting the press and measuring first moulded fittings.
**Use** daily AI manual search with approved-sheet checks.
**Save** fresh full-month night wages after bills.
feel: **Calm** because present press work and household income remain secure.
S0.quote: A spreadsheet can order resin, but it cannot make a short fitting fit a pipe.
fieldNote: His **mid-level skill** is adjusting ordinary mould cycles and finding defects, while a fitter handles electrical faults.
His **daily AI use** is established manual search; new saving comes from future paid wages, not existing reserves.

steps.text: Keep setting moulding press and measuring first fittings
Save new full-month night wages after bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the press team that an AI resin schedule may change before a robot can clear the mould. I would volunteer for a paid guarded camera test on scrap fittings, provided we see the proposed night roster too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I like learning controls, but a camera might let the plant combine night runs and reduce the premium that makes my wage high. A year saved and Clara's pay buy time, not a reason to ignore a lower rate. My daily manual searches do not teach me how to use a new reject screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the proposed roster and an offered paid trial with the setter. If a guarded practice place is offered, I would learn the AI defect-alert display by comparing good, flashed and short scrap fittings with the gauge. If paid night hours actually fall, I would apply only to posted safe nearby plastics-machine jobs whose guaranteed base pay after travel and shifts covers our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about losing night pay, even though the camera interests me. I would test the defect alert before trusting it with a paid shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What defects would the screen have to catch?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would feed a fitting with flash at the seam and one with an unfilled corner beside a good part. The setter would keep guards shut while I compare each flag with a gauge and the approved tolerance.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make another plant acceptable?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I need an actual posting with safe duties, guaranteed base pay after travel and a shift Clara and I can live around. I would not count an optional production bonus as rent money.

say: I would volunteer for a **paid guarded trial** with the proposed roster visible.
The **AI defect screen** must match gauged scrap fittings.
think: Combined **night runs** could remove part of my higher wage.
One year **saved** buys time but not a permanent premium.
do: **Request** proposed night roster and an offered guarded paid trial.
**Learn** AI defect alerts only if supervised scrap-fitting practice is offered.
**Apply** after cuts to posted safe local plastics work at bill-covering net pay.
feel: **Anxious** about plausible night-rate loss while keen to test controls.
S1.quote: I would test the defect alert before trusting it with a paid shift.
fieldNote: His **new AI learning** is active guarded defect-screen practice on paid scrap, beyond routine daily manual searches.
A **job change** requires actual hours lost and a safe local posting with guaranteed base pay after travel.

steps.text: Request proposed night roster and offered paid guarded camera trial
Learn AI defect alerts only if supervised guarded scrap practice offered
Apply after cuts to posted safe local plastics work if net base pay fits

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell Clara that AGI could plan fitting orders in 2028, while capable robots to load resin and clear the mould arrive around 2031. I would ask the plant which paid press posts remain and what practical training it will offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 63 at the robot date. I expect many physical press shifts, perhaps mine, to disappear; even other plastics shops may use the same machines. A year saved and Clara's wage give us a runway, but losing the higher night rate could change what retirement costs we can cover.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would postpone buying a second car and keep that money available for bills. I would take a locally accepted mould-quality certificate only if fees and release hours are funded and a trainer offers guarded supervised practice at a stopped press. After passing and losing shifts, I would apply to posted safe local quality jobs only if guaranteed pay after travel and shift times covers our costs; if no course place opens, I would apply to posted safe plastics-machine jobs on the same terms while keeping paid work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, with a clear reason to prepare. A quality course worth taking teaches on a safe press and leads to a real posted job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What should the practical part teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would measure a short fitting, reject a flashed one and isolate the press before clearing the mould. A qualified setter should watch me on a guarded stopped machine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you stop working at 63?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if written retirement income, Clara's dependable pay and our savings reliably cover housing, food and health costs. We have not checked those figures, so I would keep a real job search open.

say: I would distinguish **2028 order AGI** from physical moulding robots around 2031.
The plant should identify **retained paid posts** and practical training.
think: At **63**, physical press shifts and the night premium could disappear.
A one-year **reserve** and Clara's wage give time but not guaranteed retirement.
do: **Postpone** buying a second car and protect money for bills.
**Take** accepted funded paid guarded mould-quality training if offered.
**Apply** after cuts to posted safe quality if qualified, or plastics fallback, at viable net pay.
feel: **Anxious** about material night-wage loss despite a strong cushion.
S2.quote: A quality course worth taking teaches on a safe press and leads to a real posted job.
fieldNote: His **2031 robot concern** is physical press loading and clearing after AGI first affects order planning.
Both **quality and fallback searches** require real safe local postings with guaranteed wages after travel and shifts covering costs.

steps.text: Postpone second car and retain money for household bills
Take accepted quality course only if funded paid guarded stopped-press place offered
Apply after cuts to posted local quality if qualified or plastics otherwise at viable net pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AGI may plan fitting orders in 2031 while capable robots reach the press around 2034. Five years gives me time to see which local employers accept a practical quality qualification.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 66 when those robots arrive. Clara and I could stop earlier if written retirement income covers all our costs, but I do not want to count on an unverified age payment. The high night wage and year's reserve let me choose a course with real workshop hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would add new wages from full paid night months to savings after household bills. I would ask nearby plastics plants which quality certificate their current postings accept; if a funded place provides paid release and supervised guarded practice on a stopped press, I would enrol. After passing and losing hours, I would apply to posted safe local quality jobs only if guaranteed pay after travel and shift times covers costs; without a course place, I would apply to posted safe moulding-machine jobs on the same terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about whether retirement sums work, but I can use the lead time well. A workshop certificate should mean something to a hiring shop.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you decide the training is recognised?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would match the certificate name to two current quality postings and ask the employers about supervised press practice. If they do not accept it, I would keep my paid shift and seek a recognised place.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave before 2034 if the figures work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yes, if written retirement income with Clara's reliable pay covers housing, food, travel and health costs, I would stop before robots remove the shift. If not, I would continue paid work and applications.

A **five-year interval** allows real workshop training and income checks.
think: At **66**, stopping early requires reliable written retirement income.
The current **night premium** and one-year reserve permit careful choices.

fieldNote: His **new saving** draws from future paid night shifts, rather than relabelled existing reserves.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AGI could plan fittings in 2036 while capable robots reach the physical press around 2039. Ten years gives Clara and me time to compare retirement income with costs before a machine timetable sets our choice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 71 when those robots arrive, if I still work. Our current night wage, Clara's earnings and a year's reserve make the present secure, and I hope to stop before 2039. That depends on written income covering housing and health costs, not an assumed birthday payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep taking safe paid press shifts and request written retirement-income estimates beside a cost list this year. If I still need wages, I would enrol in an accepted mould-quality course only if fees, paid release and guarded supervised practice are funded. If I remain at work after 2036 and paid hours fall, I would apply only to posted safe nearby plastics or quality jobs with guaranteed base pay after travel and shifts that cover our costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the distant decision while this year's bills are covered. I prefer a work plan with numbers to an argument about a retirement age.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you put in the cost comparison?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Clara and I would list housing, groceries, travel and likely health costs against written income. Our grown children's earnings belong to their own households, not our budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a course still matter if you stop?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I would enrol only if we still need my wage and an actual funded paid guarded place is offered. If retirement income covers us, I would stop before the robot change instead.

Written **retirement income** should guide whether work continues.
think: At **71**, I may have stopped if income covers costs.
The **current night wage** and one-year reserve secure near-term living.
do: **Keep** safe paid press shifts and request written retirement figures.

feel: **Uneasy** about a future choice while current bills remain covered.
S4.quote: I prefer a work plan with numbers to an argument about a retirement age.
fieldNote: His **conditional early stop** requires reliable written income covering household and health costs, not an assumed age entitlement.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The fast 2028 AGI and 2031 robot picture is hardest because it could remove my higher paid night press shift before Clara and I know whether stopping is affordable. A funded hands-on quality place accepted nearby, posted safe jobs with enough guaranteed pay after travel, and written staffing dates would help. I would keep earning while I tested a real route.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask how a poor moulded fitting gets into a wall before anyone notices. A fast press is no bargain when a pipe joint leaks in a family's kitchen.

headlineQuote: A fast press is no bargain when a pipe joint leaks in a family's kitchen.
portrait: **Karl**, 58, is an experienced mid-level injection-moulding press operator with a vocational certificate and average machine skill.
He and his **wife Clara** have grown children, higher night pay, about a year's expenses saved and plenty of nearby plastics factories.
He uses **AI daily** for manuals and fault notes, checks real fittings and values hands-on paid apprenticeships.
Possible **2031 physical robots** threaten his premium shift; stopping work depends on written retirement income covering costs.
biggestWorry: **2031 moulding robots** could remove his higher paid night shift before replacement wages or retirement income are verified.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **accepted funded workshop training**, posted safe local jobs with adequate net pay and written staffing dates.
